speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the rash in more detail, such as its appearance, distribution, and when it first appeared? Also, have you noticed any other symptoms like joint pain or sore throat?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: The facial rash sparing the perioral area suggests a "slapped cheek" appearance, which is characteristic of Erythema Infectiosum. Do you see any pale areas around her mouth, and has the rash on her body developed a lacy or net-like pattern?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of a "slapped cheek" facial rash and a lacy, pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities following mild flu-like symptoms is classic for Erythema Infectiosum. I will confirm this clinical diagnosis with a specific serology test. REQUEST TEST: Parvovirus B19 IgM
